basis: Marrow injury defines usual acute radiation syndrome; dermal atrophy occurs in 80-99%. Common vomiting/diarrhea do not establish destructive gastrointestinal syndrome.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: vomiting and diarrhea occur in 30-79%, but destructive intestinal injury is a higher-dose manifestation without evidence of a >=30% frequency.
decisions.dermatologic: involved: direct cutaneous injury is supported by dermal atrophy in 80-99%; skin injury does not define the usual systemic syndrome.

basis: Benign reactive proliferation of lymphoid follicles; the definition overrides the lymphoma parent. Associated Hodgkin lymphoma is a separate disease.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: reactive follicular hyperplasia alone does not establish infection, immunodeficiency, autoimmune disease or lymphoma.

basis: Immune-mediated mast-cell activation is a leukocyte disorder. Episodic mediator symptoms do not establish additional organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: primary: the disease is defined by abnormal activation of mast cells, a leukocyte lineage; clonal proliferation is not required.

basis: Brain and ocular abnormalities define syndrome; hearing impairment and anemia each occur in 80-99%. Skin hypopigmentation and immune abnormalities omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.haematologic: involved: hypochromic anemia occurs in 80-99%; retained over pigmentation changes because it represents greater functional impairment.
decisions.dermatologic: none under cap: generalized hypopigmentation occurs in 80-99%, but brain, ocular, hearing and blood abnormalities take priority by functional severity.

basis: Immunodeficiency and pancytopenia occur in 4/4; learning/developmental deficits in 3/4 and hemivertebrae in 2/2. Dermatitis in 2/4 omitted at cap; infections are secondary diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: pancytopenia and anemia in 4/4 establish a core blood-cell disorder alongside the immunodeficiency.

basis: The named syndrome comprises corneal crystalline pathology, myopathy and neuropathy. No definition or phenotype data clarify the corneal findings or support additional axes.

decisions.ocular: primary: corneal pathology is a defining component of the named syndrome; the record does not establish that these are non-impairing incidental deposits.

basis: Myopathy with defining ptosis/ophthalmoplegia in 7/7; leukoencephalopathy occurs in 3/6. Retinopathy is 2/7; dysphagia reflects muscle weakness.

decisions.ocular: primary: ptosis and ophthalmoplegia are defining functional abnormalities in 7/7; eyelids are explicitly within the ocular axis.

basis: Intellectual disability, strabismus and structural limb/joint abnormalities are obligate defining findings. Obesity alone does not establish intrinsic endocrine or metabolic organ dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: obesity in 80-99% does not by itself demonstrate direct endocrine injury or an intrinsic metabolic disorder; separately coded obesity is insufficient.

basis: Ocular malformations/blindness, hypotrichosis and intellectual disability define syndrome. Dental abnormalities occur in 80-99% and occupy the fourth axis; hearing loss is occasional.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: structural dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%; teeth are gastrointestinal. The three primary slots prioritize blindness, hair abnormalities and intellectual disability.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is explicitly part of the disease definition and occurs in 80-99%; retained among the three primary axes.

basis: Hepatic heme-synthesis disorders; photosensitive skin injury affects >30% of clinical cases because cutanea tarda predominates. Neurologic injury is restricted to acute subtypes.

decisions.dermatologic: involved: damaging photosensitivity exceeds approximately 30% across clinically manifest hepatic porphyrias, with cutanea tarda the predominant form.
